Petsitter puppy abuse

By: Annalise Lubbe | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
When a young couple from Hermanus left their Boxer puppy in the care of pet sitters little did she know what horror would befell her puppy in her absence. Carte Blanche brings you the story.

Unique Selling Point:
Pet sitters have become the preferred choice for thousands of pet owners when going away. But as many people cash in on a quick buck to make in the comfort of someone else’s home, pet sitters have become a dime a dozen with some being of the worst kind. This is a story of a Boxer puppy’s abuse at the hand of an unscrupulous pet sitting couple who, over a single weekend, traumatised the animal again and again.

Summary:
A video of a couple abusing a puppy has gone viral. The couple implicated in the abuse scandal are pet sitters who offer their services in Hermanus area. The video, released by the pet owner, shows a man hitting the puppy with an object and a woman complaining. The dog is then grabbed viciously by the flesh of its neck and tossed outside. The owner is very traumatised by the incident and has seeked legal assistance after reporting the case to the SPCA. The couple was charged with animal cruelty and the case will appear in the Magistrate court in Hermanus on the 26th of April.


Further information:
It was a weekend in March when Mel Coltman, a young woman from Hermanus, made plans to go away and needed a pet sitter for her young Boxer puppy, Hector. Kennels were not an option as that would take Hector into an unfamiliar space with no personalised attention. A pet sitter was the answer. Hector would be at home with sights and smells that would make the separation more bearable, she thought. She also had the assurance of CCTV cameras in her home with real time recording.

She scanned the local community Facebook page for pet sitters and found this advert: “We look after your house and pets as your own:” the words seem comforting and reassuring. This was the advert from Natasha Koekemoer and Nazeem Salies, advertising their pet sitting services and the price they charge. She called them up to make the arrangements for the weekend.

On her return three days later, Coltman viewed the CCTV footage and was horrified at what she saw on camera: her puppy was beaten with an object on several occasions, grabbed by the neck and tossed out. In some of the footage she could see how Hector tried to find safety in his basket in the lounge, only to be man-handled and shouted at again. The abuse was constant. She immediately posted a message on the community Facebook page warning people about Koekemoer and Salies and their despicable behaviour towards Hector. She also posted a video of some of the footage which went viral.

Former President Nelson Mandela’s private secretary, Zelda le Grange, who also lives in Hermanus, saw the post. She raised the alarm and posted the video on Twitter to warn others who use the sitter’s services. Le Grange gathered the support of the members of the Hermanus community at court when the petsitters appeared in March and plans to do the same on the 26th of April when Carte Blanche has requested permission to film the court hearing. Le Grange is looking into the regulation of pet sitters in the industry to prevent abuse and has offered to arrange for a dog therapist for Hector.

There are currently only a handful companies who offer a professional pet sitter service, says Leigh de Wet, CEO of Petsitters Cape Town. The company has been running for several years and have built up a reputation for providing a selection of pet sitters who are diligent and trusted to look after a range of pets in the comfort of the home environment where pets are familiar with their routine and surroundings.

The SPCA has laid charges of animal cruelty against both Salies and Koekemoer in terms of the Animals Protection Act. Coltman is receiving legal counsel from a pro bono lawyer. The case will appear in the Hermanus Magistrate court on the 26th of April.

The story:
Our leading character is Hector the Boxer puppy and the abuse he suffered at the hands of the petsitters. We interview his owner, Mel Coltman; Jaco Pieterse, Chief Inspector from the SPCA about the charges; Zelda le Grange who came out in support; Theresa van Graan who had a negative experience with the same petsitters; and an interview with Leigh de Wet, the CEO of Petsitters Cape Town - a professional pet sitting company in the Western Cape who offers a reliable and trustworthy service to talk about their pet sitters who are screened, certified and trained and come with recommendations of pet owners who can vouch for their service. Carte Blanche have asked permission to film the abusers, Nazeem Salies and Natasha Koekemoer in court when they appear on 26 April.

Press Release:


Justice for Hector

It was a protest against the abuse of a vulnerable puppy that saw a Western Cape community rise up to take a stand outside court after a video clip of the dog being mistreated by its pet sitters went viral on social media. In an unregulated industry that is not formalised around professional standards, the SPCA intervened and launched an investigation. Carte Blanche examines how the precedent has challenged how an industry is set up and previews what a possible conviction in the ensuing court case might mean for the accused and other pet sitters.

Producer: Annalise Lubbe | Presenter: Masa Kekana

Script:


Final Script: Petsitter puppy abuse
Date: 6 May 2021
Duration: 10 minutes

LINK: When one thinks of Hermanus one thinks of whale watching. It’s a town known for its love for animals but in March this year a shocking video went viral that left the community outraged.

Up audio: chanting; ‘Justice for Hector’

V/O This is a recording of two petsitters abusing a 7-month-old Boxer puppy captured on a surveillance camera in a house in Hermanus. .

CCTV video clip

V/O Hector was only eight weeks old when he came to live with his pet-parents, Mel Coltman and Patrick Carmody in Hermanus. He soon settled in and learnt his safe space: his bed. A surveillance camera in the lounge gave Coltman peace of mind at night to monitor his movements on her cellphone.

Masa Kekana: What kind of personality does he have?

Mel Coltman: Hector’s pet-parent: Very, very laid-back especially for a Boxer, as far as Boxer’s go, very relaxed puppy.

Masa Kekana: Like most puppies they need routine and structure to get them familiar with the environment, what kind of routine did you get Hector involved in to get him more disciplined?

Mel Coltman: Well other than the feeding routine morning and evening we did focus on him waiting for his food, and then he had a fixed routine on going outside in the evenings before bed to go to the toilet to go wee. We started with his walking, he has always walked very well on a leash, very relaxed on his leash.

V/O Then in February the couple needed a petsitter when Coltman went to hospital for the birth of their baby. She called Natasha Koekemoer and Nazeem Salies, who on the community Facebook page advertise their house and petsitting services with the pay-off line: “We look after your house and pets as our own.” Comforting words when looking for someone caring and reliable. They came for a ‘meet and greet’.

Mel Coltman: They came across very friendly, very calm energy, they were great with Hector, and they said that they have got references.

V/O They were given clear instructions regarding Hector’s feeding routine, his toilet habits at night before going to bed and his essential daily walks. There were no incidents with Hector reported during their first visit. The couple therefore felt comfortable to book them again for a weekend in March. The weekend went by without a word from the petsitters till that last morning.

Mel Coltman: On the day that we were returning I got a whatsapp message from Natasha saying they left our carpet outside because Hector had weed on it. This was very strange, he had never done it before and I asked her why what happened? And she mentioned that he refused to go out to wee.

V/O This raised a red flag. Coltman logged onto her phone to view the CCTV camera footage.

Masa Kekana: And what did you see?

Mel Coltman: We saw Hector being repeatedly beaten on his bed with a plastic stick to the point that it broke on his back; other than that we also saw how he tried to get away from the situation, tried to remove himself out of his bed which is his safe place and he went into the living room around the coffee table and I think that is actually where he weed on the mat and it is out of fear. Nazeem followed him, beating him again with another stick which also broke.

Up sound

Masa Kekana: Mel, when you saw this footage what went through your mind?

Mel Coltman: I think it is just shocking, devastation, this innate kill that you left your dog with someone who would do this.

V/O Coltman asked the petsitters why Hector was beaten and this was Koekemoer’s response.

Mel Coltman: Yes, Hector did get a hiding for what he had done and that’s fine. She used the term “dis reg, dis als reg”.

V/O Beating Hector in the safety of his bed was the last straw. Coltman warned the petsitters that she would be posting the video clip on social media. Zelda La Grange, once the private secretary of President Nelson Mandela, now living in Hermanus, happened to be online.

Zelda La Grange - Concerned citizen: I saw people threatening wanting to take matters into their own hands and I decided to do something to diffuse the situation by telling people that we can lay charges, we can contact the SPCA.

Masa Kekana: And you were quite instrumental in getting people to protest peacefully outside the court. Why do you think that is also significant?

Zelda La Grange: If we don’t attend to the small issues they become big issues. There is so much abuse of vulnerable beings and that includes animals and that needs to stop. So it has to start somewhere and by publicly protesting we show people that we care.

V/O The video went viral and within 48 hours Senior Inspector Jaco Pieters from the SPCA Cape of Good Hope launched an investigation. He went to see Hector and the owners and asked for a copy of the CCTV footage.

Masa Kekana: How many times did you see Hector abused in the CCTV footage?

Jaco Pieterse: Senior Inspector SPCA - There were numerous incidents where Hector was abused in various degrees, some very serious and others just a mild abuse but at the end of the day abuse is abuse and Hector did not deserve to be abused by the very two people that were paid to look after him and care for him. Animal cruelty is a serious crime and the reason why it is serious is because animal cruelty leads to other more serious crimes.

Masa Kekana: What was Hector’s behaviour like when you went to visit the pet owners?

Jaco Pieterse: 09;58;33;10 Well the first thing is Hector is still a puppy and he is actually a lovable puppy that just wants love and attention and I had not seen any aggression in him whatsoever. I performed various examinations on him from a behaviour point of view to establish if the dog is actually aggressive. And in my opinion he had no tendencies or showed any tendencies of being aggressive whatsoever.

V/O Hector was abused repeatedly at different times over that weekend.

V/O Pieterse paid the petsitters a visit at a house in Hawston. They refused to answer any questions and he was told to leave the property. With the evidence at hand against them Pieterse opened a case of animal cruelty in terms of the Animal Protection Act. On the 29th of March Salies and Koekemoer appeared in the Magistrate court in Hermanus and were back on the 26th of April, this time with their defense attorney.

Up sound

LINK: As you can hear the chanting behind me “justice for Hector”, the community here in Hermanus is outraged by what is going on here today. The two accused just made their way into the court, we ran across the road to have a word with them but they made sure not to talk to us.

V/O Inside the court Salies and Koekemoer were called to the witness box where the Magistrate Nolan Lendor, read the charge of Animal Cruelty Act brought against the accused. An extension was granted as both the defense and the state needed more time to prepare for the case and review the CCTV footage. The court was adjourned and Salies and Koekemoer left the court with their defense attorney, Shagan Balram.

Masa Kekana Is there any way we can talk to your client?

Shagan Balram: Defense attorney - Unfortunately not. You can speak to me. They did not want to go into the merits of the matter as it is their right to remain silent at this stage.

Masa Kekana: Would you say your client is innocent?

Shagan Balram: It’s my client’s instructions that they are not guilty of the offense that they are charged and that is why I am here to provide them with the best possible defense to deal with the matter and its merits in due course.

Masa Kekana: Caitlyn when you heard about the story about Hector how did it make you feel?

Protestor: It was really emotional for me because this is my town, because this is right here.

Protestor: I actually went hot and cold to be honest; I was just frozen in time and heart broken.

Masa Kekana: What changes would you like to see in petsitting industry?

Zelda La Grange: I am at the moment also speaking to people to try and develop an app to try and regulate it in some way because anyone and his mother can now become a petsitter.

V/O Leigh de Wet runs a professional petsitting company in Cape Town. He believes the industry should be formalised.

Leigh de Wet: Founder Petsitters Cape Town: Someone can’t just walk off the street and join us. There is a contractual process in place that we have with all our petsitters; we do check for criminal records; you need to know that they are stable, that they are competent and that they are going to be reliable.

Masa Kekana; Do your services differ from individuals who advertise themselves as petsitters?

Leigh de Wet: The real differentiation comes in that we trained to do specific petsitting both in first aid, in safety first, animal behaviour and we generally know a lot more about our client and their pet’s needs than the informal side.

Up sound….”Good boy hector”

V/O Hector’s saving grace is his loving pet-family and with time he might overcome his anxiety and the abuse he suffered.

Masa Kekana: Did you notice a change in behaviour?

Mel Coltman: There is definitely a fear of us leaving the house because everytime we come back he is in a state of panic. That’s one of the behaviours we have seen and he is currently on anti-anxiety medication on a daily basis.

V/O Salies and Koekemoer will be back in court on the 11th of June.

Jaco Pieterse: If they are found guilty, they could be sentenced to a fine of up to R40 000 and or jail time of up to 12 months on each count. The magistrate can also impose a restriction on them on owning animals again and they could get a criminal record.

Masa Kekana: This case is now before the court, what outcome would you like to see?

Mel Coltman: I think we just want justice to be served for Hector. But that is up to the justice system to decide.

Mel Coltman: I think it is just shocking, devastation, this innate kill that you left your dog with someone who would do this. V/O Coltman asked the petsitters why Hector was beaten and this was Koekemoer’s response. Mel Coltman: Yes, Hector did get a hiding for what he had done and that’s fine. She used the term “dis reg, dis als reg”. V/O Beating Hector in the safety of his bed was the last straw. Coltman warned the petsitters that she would be posting the video clip on social media. Zelda La Grange, once the private secretary of President Nelson Mandela, now living in Hermanus, happened to be online. Zelda La Grange - Concerned citizen: I saw people threatening wanting to take matters into their own hands and I decided to do something to diffuse the situation by telling people that we can lay charges, we can contact the SPCA. Masa Kekana: And you were quite instrumental in getting people to protest peacefully outside the court. Why do you think that is also significant? Zelda La Grange: If we don’t attend to the small issues they become big issues. There is so much abuse of vulnerable beings and that includes animals and that needs to stop. So it has to start somewhere and by publicly protesting we show people that we care. V/O The video went viral and within 48 hours Senior Inspector Jaco Pieters from the SPCA Cape of Good Hope launched an investigation. He went to see Hector and the owners and asked for a copy of the CCTV footage. Masa Kekana: How many times did you see Hector abused in the CCTV footage? Jaco Pieterse: Senior Inspector SPCA - There were numerous incidents where Hector was abused in various degrees, some very serious and others just a mild abuse but at the end of the day abuse is abuse and Hector did not deserve to be abused by the very two people that were paid to look after him and care for him. Animal cruelty is a serious crime and the reason why it is serious is because animal cruelty leads to other more serious crimes. Masa Kekana: What was Hector’s behaviour like when you went to visit the pet owners? Jaco Pieterse: 09;58;33;10 Well the first thing is Hector is still a puppy and he is actually a lovable puppy that just wants love and attention and I had not seen any aggression in him whatsoever. I performed various examinations on him from a behaviour point of view to establish if the dog is actually aggressive. And in my opinion he had no tendencies or showed any tendencies of being aggressive whatsoever. V/O Hector was abused repeatedly at different times over that weekend. V/O Pieterse paid the petsitters a visit at a house in Hawston. They refused to answer any questions and he was told to leave the property. With the evidence at hand against them Pieterse opened a case of animal cruelty in terms of the Animal Protection Act. On the 29th of March Salies and Koekemoer appeared in the Magistrate court in Hermanus and were back on the 26th of April, this time with their defense attorney. Up sound LINK: As you can hear the chanting behind me “justice for Hector”, the community here in Hermanus is outraged by what is going on here today. The two accused just made their way into the court, we ran across the road to have a word with them but they made sure not to talk to us. V/O Inside the court Salies and Koekemoer were called to the witness box where the Magistrate Nolan Lendor, read the charge of Animal Cruelty Act brought against the accused. An extension was granted as both the defense and the state needed more time to prepare for the case and review the CCTV footage. The court was adjourned and Salies and Koekemoer left the court with their defense attorney, Shagan Balram. Masa Kekana Is there any way we can talk to your client? Shagan Balram: Defense attorney - Unfortunately not. You can speak to me. They did not want to go into the merits of the matter as it is their right to remain silent at this stage. Masa Kekana: Would you say your client is innocent? Shagan Balram: It’s my client’s instructions that they are not guilty of the offense that they are charged and that is why I am here to provide them with the best possible defense to deal with the matter and its merits in due course. Masa Kekana: Caitlyn when you heard about the story about Hector how did it make you feel? Protestor: It was really emotional for me because this is my town, because this is right here. Protestor: I actually went hot and cold to be honest; I was just frozen in time and heart broken. Masa Kekana: What changes would you like to see in petsitting industry? Zelda La Grange: I am at the moment also speaking to people to try and develop an app to try and regulate it in some way because anyone and his mother can now become a petsitter. V/O Leigh de Wet runs a professional petsitting company in Cape Town. He believes the industry should be formalised. Leigh de Wet: Founder Petsitters Cape Town: Someone can’t just walk off the street and join us. There is a contractual process in place that we have with all our petsitters; we do check for criminal records; you need to know that they are stable, that they are competent and that they are going to be reliable. Masa Kekana; Do your services differ from individuals who advertise themselves as petsitters? Leigh de Wet: The real differentiation comes in that we trained to do specific petsitting both in first aid, in safety first, animal behaviour and we generally know a lot more about our client and their pet’s needs than the informal side. Up sound….”Good boy hector” V/O Hector’s saving grace is his loving pet-family and with time he might overcome his anxiety and the abuse he suffered. Masa Kekana: Did you notice a change in behaviour? Mel Coltman: There is definitely a fear of us leaving the house because everytime we come back he is in a state of panic. That’s one of the behaviours we have seen and he is currently on anti-anxiety medication on a daily basis. V/O Salies and Koekemoer will be back in court on the 11th of June. Jaco Pieterse: If they are found guilty, they could be sentenced to a fine of up to R40 000 and or jail time of up to 12 months on each count. The magistrate can also impose a restriction on them on owning animals again and they could get a criminal record. Masa Kekana: This case is now before the court, what outcome would you like to see? Mel Coltman: I think we just want justice to be served for Hector. But that is up to the justice system to decide. ____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Promo 1 When a couple from Hermanus went away for the weekend, the petsitters they trusted to look after their beloved animal, turned out to be abusing their seven-month-old Boxer puppy. Pomo 2 Two petsitters from Hermanus were charged with animal cruelty for repeatedly beating a seven-month-old Boxer puppy placed in their care while the owners were away for the weekend. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): When a young couple from Hermanus left their Boxer puppy in the care of pet sitters little did she know what horror would befell her puppy in her absence. Carte Blanche brings you the story.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Pet sitters have become the preferred choice for thousands of pet owners when going away. But as many people cash in on a quick buck to make in the comfort of someone else’s home, pet sitters have become a dime a dozen with some being of the worst kind. This is a story of a Boxer puppy’s abuse at the hand of an unscrupulous pet sitting couple who, over a single weekend, traumatised the animal again and again.
metadata.Summary: A video of a couple abusing a puppy has gone viral. The couple implicated in the abuse scandal are pet sitters who offer their services in Hermanus area. The video, released by the pet owner, shows a man hitting the puppy with an object and a woman complaining. The dog is then grabbed viciously by the flesh of its neck and tossed outside. The owner is very traumatised by the incident and has seeked legal assistance after reporting the case to the SPCA. The couple was charged with animal cruelty and the case will appear in the Magistrate court in Hermanus on the 26th of April.
metadata.Further information: It was a weekend in March when Mel Coltman, a young woman from Hermanus, made plans to go away and needed a pet sitter for her young Boxer puppy, Hector. Kennels were not an option as that would take Hector into an unfamiliar space with no personalised attention. A pet sitter was the answer. Hector would be at home with sights and smells that would make the separation more bearable, she thought. She also had the assurance of CCTV cameras in her home with real time recording. She scanned the local community Facebook page for pet sitters and found this advert: “We look after your house and pets as your own:” the words seem comforting and reassuring. This was the advert from Natasha Koekemoer and Nazeem Salies, advertising their pet sitting services and the price they charge. She called them up to make the arrangements for the weekend. On her return three days later, Coltman viewed the CCTV footage and was horrified at what she saw on camera: her puppy was beaten with an object on several occasions, grabbed by the neck and tossed out. In some of the footage she could see how Hector tried to find safety in his basket in the lounge, only to be man-handled and shouted at again. The abuse was constant. She immediately posted a message on the community Facebook page warning people about Koekemoer and Salies and their despicable behaviour towards Hector. She also posted a video of some of the footage which went viral. Former President Nelson Mandela’s private secretary, Zelda le Grange, who also lives in Hermanus, saw the post. She raised the alarm and posted the video on Twitter to warn others who use the sitter’s services. Le Grange gathered the support of the members of the Hermanus community at court when the petsitters appeared in March and plans to do the same on the 26th of April when Carte Blanche has requested permission to film the court hearing. Le Grange is looking into the regulation of pet sitters in the industry to prevent abuse and has offered to arrange for a dog therapist for Hector. There are currently only a handful companies who offer a professional pet sitter service, says Leigh de Wet, CEO of Petsitters Cape Town. The company has been running for several years and have built up a reputation for providing a selection of pet sitters who are diligent and trusted to look after a range of pets in the comfort of the home environment where pets are familiar with their routine and surroundings. The SPCA has laid charges of animal cruelty against both Salies and Koekemoer in terms of the Animals Protection Act. Coltman is receiving legal counsel from a pro bono lawyer. The case will appear in the Hermanus Magistrate court on the 26th of April. The story: Our leading character is Hector the Boxer puppy and the abuse he suffered at the hands of the petsitters. We interview his owner, Mel Coltman; Jaco Pieterse, Chief Inspector from the SPCA about the charges; Zelda le Grange who came out in support; Theresa van Graan who had a negative experience with the same petsitters; and an interview with Leigh de Wet, the CEO of Petsitters Cape Town - a professional pet sitting company in the Western Cape who offers a reliable and trustworthy service to talk about their pet sitters who are screened, certified and trained and come with recommendations of pet owners who can vouch for their service. Carte Blanche have asked permission to film the abusers, Nazeem Salies and Natasha Koekemoer in court when they appear on 26 April. ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
